search_log: Searched “The Covenant of Water Abraham Verghese excerpt first chapter publisher” and opened the Grove Atlantic authorized opening.
Searched “The Covenant of Water third person narrator” and “The Covenant of Water point of view narration”; opened explicit whole-book descriptions from BookRags and GradeSaver.
Searched the publisher domain for an excerpt and opened the Oprah Daily publisher-permitted interior Digby extract.
Searched “The Covenant of Water epistolary diary first person sections” and found no credible evidence of sustained first-person base sections.

Searched exact first-person quote fragments including “I have been bent and broken,” “I am so behind that yesterday catches up with tomorrow,” and “Whatever is next for me”; results indicated isolated quotation, thought, or journal material rather than a first-person controlling narrator.
Reviewed a Barnes & Noble author interview discussing shifts among Big Ammachi’s and Digby’s viewpoints; it corroborated changing focalization but was not treated as grammatical-person evidence.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating third person, with omniscient or flexible limited focalization across several characters. The quote set repeatedly shows sustained third-person access to characters such as Digby, Rune, Big Ammachi, and Mariamma, and this agrees with authorized excerpts from both the opening and an interior Digby section. Independent whole-book guides explicitly describe third-person omniscient narration as consistent throughout. Isolated first-person lines are aphorisms, speech, direct thought, quotation, or journal material and therefore do not constitute autonomous first-person base sections. No credible evidence of alternating grammatical person was found; the only minor uncertainty is that many popularity-selected quotes are too short or gnomic to be individually diagnostic.
